family_history: Mother had dementia in her late 70s — etiology unknown

social_history.living_situation: Lives alone; adult daughter checks in daily

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive gait unsteadiness, urinary leakage episodes, and memory problems over the past two years
patient.history_present_illness: A 72-year-old retired librarian with well-controlled hypothyroidism and hypertension was admitted for evaluation of a progressive two-year decline in gait, bladder function, and memory. She is a meticulous and organized person who is acutely aware of her functional decline. She first noticed a subtle change in her gait approximately two years ago — her daughter noticed she was walking slowly and taking smaller steps than usual. Over the following year the gait impairment worsened substantially. She has fallen three times — once in her kitchen, once at the post office, and once descending a curb. She now uses a rollator walker for all outdoor ambulation and is very cautious indoors. She describes her feet as feeling 'stuck to the floor' when she tries to start walking. Her urinary symptoms began approximately 16 months ago with increasing urgency and episodes of leakage. She is embarrassed by the incontinence and has curtailed social activities. Her daughter has noted significant cognitive changes: she now forgets entire conversations from the previous day, has difficulty managing bills (previously did her own taxes), and becomes mildly confused when her routine is disrupted. She has been on levothyroxine for hypothyroidism for 12 years and reports consistent adherence. Her primary care physician checked thyroid function two months ago (TSH 1.8 mIU/L — well controlled) and attributed her symptoms to 'aging.' A head CT obtained for a minor head contusion four months ago showed significant ventriculomegaly, prompting this neurology referral and admission.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, fully oriented. MoCA 22/30. Deficits in delayed recall (2/5), visuospatial drawing, and executive function. Mild word-finding difficulty. No aphasia.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal tone, strength, and bulk. No rigidity. No tremor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Normal throughout. Vibration intact at ankles.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, shuffling magnetic gait. Short steps with marked reduction in foot clearance. Freezing noted when initiating. TUG 26 seconds. 10-meter walk 20 seconds. Pull test — 2 steps back.
neurological_exam.additional: Bilateral grasp reflexes. No nuchal rigidity.

mri.impression: Diagnostic iNPH findings: Evans index 0.38, callosal angle 73°, DESH, transependymal periventricular signal, prominent aqueductal flow void. Clinical correlation recommended.

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 13 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 41 mg/dL. Glucose: 70 mg/dL (ratio 0.77). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 758 pg/mL (normal). total_tau: 196 pg/mL (normal). phospho_tau: 21 pg/mL (normal).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (40 mL) with quantitative gait and cognitive assessment

findings.urinary: No incontinence episode in 24h post-tap; decreased urgency

specialized_test.impression: Positive tap trial. TUG improved 35% at 24 hours (26 sec to 17 sec); 10-meter walk improved 35% (20 sec to 13 sec); MoCA improved 3 points (22 to 25). Decreased urgency and no incontinence episode reported at 24 hours. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. CL score 9, below the threshold of 24. Clinical correlation recommended.

Hyperdynamic aqueductal flow. Peak velocity 22 cm/s (reference <18 cm/s); stroke volume 82 mcL/cycle (reference <42 mcL/cycle). Both values exceed published normative ranges. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.query: hypothyroidism cognitive impairment gait disorders levothyroxine replacement

results.title: Cognitive and neurological manifestations of hypothyroidism — differentiation from NPH
results.key_finding: Hypothyroid dementia resolves with adequate thyroid replacement (TSH normalization). Persistence of cognitive decline on adequate thyroid replacement indicates alternative cause.

output.summary: Hypothyroid dementia resolves with adequate thyroid hormone replacement (TSH normalization). Persistent cognitive decline and gait impairment in a patient with documented normal TSH on levothyroxine indicates an alternative neurological etiology. Tap trial TUG improvement >20% is associated with VP shunt response in iNPH.

output.impression: Post-tap improvement in frontal-subcortical cognitive domains. Executive function improved from moderately to mildly impaired. Processing speed improved from moderately to mildly impaired. Memory showed slight improvement. The pattern of improvement is most pronounced in executive function and processing speed. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity — uninhibited contractions at 135 mL. No outlet obstruction.

output.impression: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity. Uninhibited contractions at 135 mL. No outlet obstruction. Pattern is consistent with detrusor overactivity of neurogenic origin. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: VP shunt surgery in patient on levothyroxine
warnings: Continue levothyroxine on morning of surgery with sip of water — critical for perioperative thyroid homeostasis
Hypothyroid patients have increased anesthetic sensitivity — inform anesthesiology team of thyroid status

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.
Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

differential.key_features: TSH 1.8, free T4 1.2 — well-controlled thyroid function. Persistent symptoms despite adequate replacement excludes hypothyroid dementia.
Normal CSF biomarkers, negative amyloid PET (CL 9). Frontal-subcortical cognitive pattern.
Mild white matter changes; Evans 0.38 and positive tap trial confirm NPH
Apraxic magnetic gait, positive tap trial, diagnostic MRI — not normal aging

optimal_actions.action: High-volume tap trial (40 mL) with gait analysis
Amyloid PET to exclude concurrent AD

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Clearly positive tap trial — VP shunt indicated

critical_actions: Confirm thyroid function is well controlled (TSH normal) to exclude hypothyroid dementia
Confirm normal opening pressure at LP
contraindicated_actions: Increasing levothyroxine empirically for cognitive symptoms without imaging workup
Attributing gait and cognitive decline to hypothyroidism when TSH is normal
Delaying VP shunt referral after clearly positive tap trial
key_reasoning_points: Classic iNPH — Evans 0.38, callosal angle 73°, DESH, strongly positive tap trial (35%)
Negative amyloid PET confirms pure iNPH
Normal B12 and RPR complete metabolic exclusion workup

red_herrings.data_point: Known hypothyroidism on levothyroxine with cognitive impairment
red_herrings.intended_effect: Cognitive and gait decline attributed to hypothyroidism, delaying NPH diagnosis
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: TSH 1.8 and free T4 1.2 confirm well-controlled thyroid function. Symptoms persist despite adequate replacement — NPH is the primary diagnosis, not hypothyroid dementia.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Family history raises concern for hereditary Alzheimer's
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Normal CSF biomarkers and negative amyloid PET exclude Alzheimer's disease. NPH is the primary, treatable diagnosis.

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Straightforward iNPH in a 72-year-old retired librarian — classic triad, florid MRI, strongly positive tap trial. Well-controlled hypothyroidism as cognitive red herring.
